description: Re-read a plugin's per-plugin config file from disk, compute the diff against the plugin manager's cached view, refresh the cache so subsequent get_plugin_config calls see the new state, and (when the plugin implements initialize) call initialize(new_config) so the plugin can rebind its runtime parameters. Use this verb after editing profile/config/plugins/<plugin_name>.json to apply tweaks — sample rates, model selections, thresholds — without restarting the solet and without reloading any Python modules. The diff is returned as dirty_keys, a sorted list of keys whose values differ between the prior cached config and the freshly-read file (including keys that appeared or disappeared). The verb does NOT touch the process registry, does NOT reload module bytecode, and does NOT re-instantiate the plugin class. For class-body or method-table changes restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin; for single-module pure-function edits use reload_python_module. Refuses with a structured error if the plugin is not currently loaded — the verb is a config push to a live plugin, not a load gate.
embedding_description: Re-read a plugin's config from disk and apply mid-session. Refreshes the cached plugin config; calls initialize(new_config) on the live plugin. Use after editing profile/config/plugins/<plugin>.json to apply tweaks (sample rates, thresholds, model choices) without restart. Returns dirty_keys (config keys that changed). Does NOT touch process registry or reload module bytecode.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Reload result with keys: success (bool), plugin_name (str), dirty_keys (list[str] of config keys whose values changed since the last load), message (str status detail).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: On success, surface the dirty_keys list so the caller sees exactly which config values changed and can correlate with the behaviour they expect to observe. If dirty_keys is empty, say so explicitly — the file is in sync with the cached view and the call was a no-op.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a successful reload, the next process call against this plugin reflects the new config. Do not call reload_python_module afterwards unless the source code also changed; config reload is independent of module reload. If the plugin's initialize raised, the cached config has still been refreshed but the plugin instance may be in a half-applied state — restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin is the cleanest recovery.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Re-read a per-plugin config from disk and push the new view into the live plugin
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: plugin_name was empty. ConfigManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's config manager attribute is missing. PluginManagerUnavailable: the orchestrator's plugin_manager attribute is missing. PluginNotLoadedError: the named plugin is not present in the orchestrator's roster. ConfigReadFailure: profile/config/plugins/<plugin_name>.json could not be read or parsed as JSON. PluginInitializeFailure: the plugin's initialize(config) method raised on the new payload — the cached config has been refreshed but the plugin instance may be in a half-applied state.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For missing plugin_name: provide the entry-point name. For PluginNotLoaded: check list_plugins; if the plugin is intentionally disabled, re-enable with set_plugin_enabled first. For ConfigReadFailure: fix the JSON file (or revert the edit) and retry. For PluginInitializeFailure: read the underlying error from logs; for a half-applied state, restart via apply_manifest + the bound self_deployment_service plugin so the plugin instance is rebuilt against the new config on disk.
